goal: Stop the same-repo return_to loop: a returned copy must be recognisable as a copy wherever it is filed, so returning it again is refused instead of minting the next generation, without weakening the reject classification or the already-returned guard.
dispatcher: Owner Albert Hazan authorized resolving open non-orchestrator issues through to production
prohibited_actions: No database read, write, migration, or schema change of any kind.
Do not weaken or delete the NOT ORCHESTRATOR WORK reject classification or the already-returned guard.
Do not edit, close, or return issues #2690, #2691 or #2692.
Do not forbid a same-repo return_to; the owner question of whether it is legitimate is not this change's to decide.
assumptions: A same-repo return_to is legitimate: source-data-session names a session inside this repository, so the fix marks the copy rather than rejecting the address (shape 1 of the two the issue offered).
The three copies already open carry the legacy 'Returned from <owner/repo>#<n> by the shared-db orchestrator.' provenance line, so recognising that line covers them without editing them.
Generation 2 rebinds the contract after merging current main into the branch; the implementation is unchanged from generation 1 apart from the two low findings grok-4.6 raised at 9197dafb.
stop_conditions: Stop if the fix would require a database or schema change.
Stop if the only way to pass the queue audit is to weaken the reject classification.
